A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemBD research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack evaluations, defense comparisons, utility measurements, ablations, and fine-tuning robustness experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds trigger-specificity, trigger–target generalization, pruning, and random-seed evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same semantic trigger construction, substring regularization, multi-entity targets, projection editing, and training losses. The additional evaluations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V3 broadens semantic coverage through five additional trigger–target configurations and structured compositional and semantic-adjacent prompts (Tables 2, 5, 9–10). This extends the existing T2I backdoor task; MS-COCO utility data and Pokémon-caption fine-tuning data remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Pruning is newly evaluated as a model-level defense against SemBD in Section 5.6 and Table 6. The six attack baselines, four input-level detectors, and full/LoRA fine-tuning comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces category-based FTR and prompt-similarity evaluation, reporting 100 prompts per category, and a pruning-ratio sweep from 0.1 to 0.9. It also changes the stated evaluation-prompt generator from GPT-4 to GPT-5. The models, 800 optimization iterations, and 5,000-caption FID setup remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained results were recomputed.

E4.justification: V3 adds quantitative tests of compositional trigger specificity and regularization versus FTR, stability across five trigger–target pairs, pruning sensitivity, and seed robustness. These substantially expand the questions tested beyond v1's existing qualitative regularization analysis, parameter and trigger-count ablations, target-design comparison, and fine-tuning robustness.

E5.justification: V1 provides no corresponding repeated-seed reporting. V3 Appendix D reports six specified seeds for each model, with individual metric values and means. This substantially expands repeatability reporting, without establishing that earlier experiments used fewer seeds. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive specificity, trigger–target, pruning, and seed results. For example, Table 3 reports FTR of 3.04% on SDv1.5 and 5.72% on SDXL at regularization strength 0.5; Table 6 reports zero ASR at pruning ratio 0.5. In retained Table 1, benign-model FID changes from 20.59 to 24.49, while other numerical scores remain unchanged apart from equivalent formatting.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, semantic-stability analysis, and convergence argument are retained. V1 Appendices B–C correspond to v3 Appendices E–F with unchanged substantive assumptions, theorems, and derivations; differences are editorial and organizational.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, semantic-trigger, multi-entity-target, attack-success, and stealthiness claims. The conclusion also retains its claim of benign behavior under incomplete semantics. Additional experiments support or qualify existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations that excessive regularization overconstrains the trigger region and that stronger pruning suppresses the backdoor while damaging generation quality. Appendix A also distinguishes detection on triggered inputs from overall balanced-set accuracy. These qualify the evaluation while retaining the central semantic-generalization and stealthiness interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-availability link, explicit prompts for the new evaluations, and clarification that fine-tuning robustness uses SDv1.5. Table 8 also discloses a twelfth paraphrase for the already-existing Figure 12 ablation; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a newly enlarged training trigger set.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Jiang et al.'s combinational attack, Guo et al.'s TrojanEdit, and Liu et al.'s pruning defense, and replaces the GPT-4 reference with a GPT-5 reference. The related-work organization and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental discussion, reorders setup paragraphs, and reorganizes the empirical appendices. It adds acknowledgements, updates affiliations, fixes the placeholder running title, and corrects a figure reference. The overall main-section structure and method/proof exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds eight tables and the multi-pair image grid in Figure 14, substantially expanding the experimental displays and rearranging their layout. Figures 1–13 are retained. V1 Tables 2–4 correspond to v3 Tables 4, 8, and 7, with the prompt table expanded and comparison tables gaining underlined emphasis.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important gaps in v1's validation through quantitative trigger-specificity tests, evaluations across different semantic concepts, and explicit seed results. These substantially improve assessment of generality, repeatability, and failure conditions; pruning tests and fuller prompt documentation add useful support. Qualifications remain: Table 2's nonzero FTR conflicts with the retained blanket benign-behavior claim, and the new Table 3 ASR values are not reconciled with retained Figure 9.
